input.title: Add prompt-start checkpoints for better rewind granularity
input.description:
## Summary

Currently, temporary checkpoints are only created at the **stop hook** (end of agent prompt). This means user changes made before the prompt are bundled together with agent changes in a single checkpoint.

## Proposed Behavior

Create checkpoints at **both** prompt-start and stop:

| Event | Checkpoint? | Why |
|-------|-------------|-----|
| prompt-start | Only if tree changed since last checkpoint | Captures user changes |
| stop | Only if tree changed since last checkpoint | Captures agent changes |

### Example with user changes between prompts:
```
User Y → prompt-start [Y] → Agent X → stop [Y+X] → User Z → prompt-start [Y+X+Z] → Agent A → stop [Y+X+Z+A]
```

Rewind points: [Y, Y+X, Y+X+Z, Y+X+Z+A]

### Example without user changes between prompts:
```
User Y → prompt-start [Y] → Agent X → stop [Y+X] → prompt-start (skipped, same tree) → Agent A → stop [Y+X+A]
```

Rewind points: [Y, Y+X, Y+X+A] (prompt-start skipped due to deduplication)

## Benefits

- **Better rewind granularity**: Can rewind to "before agent touched it" vs "after agent finished"
- **Clearer attribution**: Separates user changes from agent changes
- **No redundant checkpoints**: Existing deduplication logic handles "no changes" case

## Notes

- These are temporary checkpoints on the shadow branch, separate from condensation to `entire/sessions`
- If user starts clean (no changes from HEAD), prompt-start checkpoint can be skipped
- Implementation should leverage existing deduplication (tree hash comparison)

## Summary

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|

| Only skips `.git/`, `.entire/` | Respects `.gitignore` |
| Includes `node_modules/`, `.worktrees/` | Excludes gitignored files |
| O(n) where n = all files | O(m) where m = changed files |

- Modified tracked files (`git.Modified`)
- Untracked non-ignored files (`git.Untracked`)
- Excludes `.entire/` via `paths.IsInfrastructurePath()`
- `.git/` is excluded automatically by git

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Re-fetch comment IDs (if rebased)

**Important:** If you rebased or force-pushed, comment IDs may have changed. Re-fetch the comment threads before replying:

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq '...'
```

### 6. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 7. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

     func collectChangedFiles(_ *git.Repository) ([]string, error) {
         ctx := context.Background()
         cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "status", "--porcelain")
         output, err := cmd.Output()
         if err != nil {

         lines := strings.Split(string(output), "\n")

             }

             staging := line[0]
             worktree := line[1]

   503→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use

   505→	// List all shadow branches

   513→	// Iterate through each shadow branch and collect checkpoints
   514→	for _, branch := range branches {

   543→// GetTranscriptFromCommit retrieves the transcript from a specific commit's tree.
   544→// This is used for shadow branch checkpoints where the transcript is stored in the commit tree
   545→// rather than on the entire/sessions branch.
   546→// commitHash is the commit to read from, metadataDir is the path within the tree.
   547→// agentType is used for reassembling chunked transcripts in the correct format.
   548→// Handles both chunked and non-chunked transcripts.
   549→func (s *GitStore) GetTranscriptFromCommit(commitHash plumbing.Hash, metadataDir string, agentType agent.AgentType) ([]byte, error) {
   550→	commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(commitHash)
   551→	if err != nil {
   552→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
   553→	}
   554→
   555→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   556→	if err != nil {
   557→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	// Try to get the metadata subtree for chunk detection
   561→	subTree, subTreeErr := tree.Tree(metadataDir)
   562→	if subTreeErr == nil {
   563→		// Use the helper function that handles chunking
   564→		transcript, err := readTranscriptFromTree(subTree, agentType)
   565→		if err == nil && transcript != nil {
   566→			return transcript, nil
   567→		}
   568→	}
   569→
   570→	// Fall back to direct file access (for backwards compatibility)
   571→	transcriptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
   572→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   573→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   574→		if contentErr == nil {
   575→			return []byte(content), nil
   576→		}
   577→	}
   578→
   579→	transcriptPath = metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy
   580→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   581→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   582→		if contentErr == nil {
   583→			return []byte(content), nil
   584→		}
   585→	}
   586→
   587→	return nil, ErrNoTranscript
   588→}

   600→// worktreeID should be empty for main worktree or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   601→func (s *GitStore) DeleteShadowBranch(baseCommit, worktreeID string) error {
   602→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID)
   603→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   604→	if err := s.repo.Storer.RemoveReference(refName); err != nil {
   605→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete shadow branch %s: %w", shadowBranchName, err)

   610→// ShadowBranchNameForCommit returns the shadow branch name for a base commit hash
   611→// and worktree identifier. The worktree ID should be empty for the main worktree
   612→// or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   613→// Format: entire/<commit[:7]>-<hash(worktreeID)[:6]>
   614→func ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID string) string {
   615→	commitPart := baseCommit
   616→	if len(baseCommit) >= ShadowBranchHashLength {
   617→		commitPart = baseCommit[:ShadowBranchHashLength]
   618→	}
   619→	worktreeHash := HashWorktreeID(worktreeID)
   620→	return ShadowBranchPrefix + commitPart + "-" + worktreeHash
   621→}
   622→
   623→// ParseShadowBranchName extracts the commit prefix and worktree hash from a shadow branch name.
   624→// Input format: "entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>"
   625→// Returns (commitPrefix, worktreeHash, ok). Returns ("", "", false) if not a valid shadow branch.
   626→func ParseShadowBranchName(branchName string) (commitPrefix, worktreeHash string, ok bool) {
   627→	if !strings.HasPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix) {
   628→		return "", "", false
   629→	}
   630→	suffix := strings.TrimPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix)
   631→
   632→	// Find the last dash - everything before is commit prefix, after is worktree hash
   633→	lastDash := strings.LastIndex(suffix, "-")
   634→	if lastDash == -1 || lastDash == 0 || lastDash == len(suffix)-1 {
   635→		// No dash, or dash at start/end - invalid format
   636→		// Could be old format "entire/<commit[:7]>" without worktree hash
   637→		return suffix, "", true // Return as commit prefix with empty worktree hash
   638→	}
   639→
   640→	return suffix[:lastDash], suffix[lastDash+1:], true
   641→}

   643→// getOrCreateShadowBranch gets or creates the shadow branch for checkpoints.
   644→// Returns (parentHash, baseTreeHash, error).
   645→func (s *GitStore) getOrCreateShadowBranch(branchName string) (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   646→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   647→	ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   648→
   649→	if err == nil {
   650→		// Branch exists
   651→		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   652→		if err != nil {
   653→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   654→		}
   655→		return ref.Hash(), commit.TreeHash, nil
   656→	}
   657→
   658→	// Branch doesn't exist, use current HEAD's tree as base
   659→	head, err := s.repo.Head()
   660→	if err != nil {
   661→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   662→	}
   663→
   664→	headCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   665→	if err != nil {
   666→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD commit: %w", err)
   667→	}
   668→
   669→	return plumbing.ZeroHash, headCommit.TreeHash, nil
   670→}

   672→// buildTreeWithChanges builds a git tree with the given changes.
   673→// metadataDir is the relative path for git tree entries, metadataDirAbs is the absolute path
   674→// for filesystem operations (needed when CLI is run from a subdirectory).
   675→func (s *GitStore) buildTreeWithChanges(
   676→	baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash,
   677→	modifiedFiles, deletedFiles []string,
   678→	metadataDir, metadataDirAbs string,
   679→) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   680→	// Get repo root for resolving file paths
   681→	// This is critical because fileExists() and createBlobFromFile() use os.Stat()
   682→	// which resolves relative to CWD. The modifiedFiles are repo-relative paths,
   683→	// so we must resolve them against repo root, not CWD.
   684→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   685→	if err != nil {
   686→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   687→	}
   688→
   689→	// Get the base tree
   690→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   691→	if err != nil {
   692→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   693→	}
   694→
   695→	// Flatten existing tree
   696→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   697→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   698→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten base tree: %w", err)
   699→	}
   700→
   701→	// Remove deleted files
   702→	for _, file := range deletedFiles {
   703→		delete(entries, file)
   704→	}
   705→
   706→	// Add/update modified files
   707→	for _, file := range modifiedFiles {
   708→		// Resolve path relative to repo root for filesystem operations
   709→		absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   710→		if !fileExists(absPath) {
   711→			delete(entries, file)
   712→			continue
   713→		}
   714→
   715→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(s.repo, absPath)
   716→		if err != nil {
   717→			// Skip files that can't be staged (may have been deleted since detection)
   718→			continue
   719→		}
   720→
   721→		entries[file] = object.TreeEntry{
   722→			Name: file,
   723→			Mode: mode,
   724→			Hash: blobHash,
   725→		}
   726→	}
   727→
   728→	// Add metadata directory files
   729→	if metadataDir != "" && metadataDirAbs != "" {
   730→		if err := addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(s.repo, metadataDirAbs, metadataDir, entries); err != nil {
   731→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to add metadata directory: %w", err)
   732→		}
   733→	}
   734→
   735→	// Build tree
   736→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   737→}

   742→	sig := object.Signature{

   748→	commit := &object.Commit{

   776→// FlattenTree recursively flattens a tree into a map of full paths to entries.
   777→func FlattenTree(repo *git.Repository, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   778→	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
   779→		fullPath := entry.Name
   780→		if prefix != "" {
   781→			fullPath = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
   782→		}
   783→
   784→		if entry.Mode == filemode.Dir {
   785→			// Recurse into subtree
   786→			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
   787→			if err != nil {
   788→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get subtree %s: %w", fullPath, err)
   789→			}
   790→			if err := FlattenTree(repo, subtree, fullPath, entries); err != nil {
   791→				return err
   792→			}
   793→		} else {
   794→			entries[fullPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   795→				Name: fullPath,
   796→				Mode: entry.Mode,
   797→				Hash: entry.Hash,
   798→			}
   799→		}
   800→	}
   801→	return nil
   802→}

   804→// fileExists checks if a file exists at the given path.

   810→// createBlobFromFile creates a blob object from a file in the working directory.
   811→func createBlobFromFile(repo *git.Repository, filePath string) (plumbing.Hash, filemode.FileMode, error) {
   812→	info, err := os.Stat(filePath)
   813→	if err != nil {
   814→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to stat file: %w", err)
   815→	}
   816→
   817→	// Determine file mode
   818→	mode := filemode.Regular
   819→	if info.Mode()&0o111 != 0 {
   820→		mode = filemode.Executable
   821→	}
   822→	if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
   823→		mode = filemode.Symlink
   824→	}
   825→
   826→	// Read file contents
   827→	content, err := os.ReadFile(filePath) //nolint:gosec // filePath comes from walking the repository
   828→	if err != nil {
   829→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read file: %w", err)
   830→	}
   831→
   832→	// Create blob object
   833→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   834→	obj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
   835→	obj.SetSize(int64(len(content)))
   836→
   837→	writer, err := obj.Writer()
   838→	if err != nil {
   839→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to get object writer: %w", err)
   840→	}
   841→
   842→	_, err = writer.Write(content)
   843→	if err != nil {
   844→		_ = writer.Close()
   845→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to write blob content: %w", err)
   846→	}
   847→	if err := writer.Close(); err != nil {
   848→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to close blob writer: %w", err)
   849→	}
   850→
   851→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   852→	if err != nil {
   853→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to store blob object: %w", err)
   854→	}
   855→
   856→	return hash, mode, nil
   857→}

   859→// addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath recursively adds all files in a directory to the entries map.
   860→func addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(repo *git.Repository, dirPathAbs, dirPathRel string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   861→	err := filepath.Walk(dirPathAbs, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
   862→		if err != nil {
   863→			return err
   864→		}
   865→		if info.IsDir() {
   866→			return nil
   867→		}
   868→
   869→		// Calculate relative path within the directory, then join with dirPathRel for tree entry
   870→		relWithinDir, err := filepath.Rel(dirPathAbs, path)
   871→		if err != nil {
   872→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get relative path for %s: %w", path, err)
   873→		}
   874→
   875→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(repo, path)
   876→		if err != nil {
   877→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create blob for %s: %w", path, err)
   878→		}
   879→
   880→		treePath := filepath.Join(dirPathRel, relWithinDir)
   881→		entries[treePath] = object.TreeEntry{
   882→			Name: treePath,
   883→			Mode: mode,
   884→			Hash: blobHash,
   885→		}
   886→		return nil
   887→	})
   888→	if err != nil {
   889→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to walk directory %s: %w", dirPathAbs, err)
   890→	}
   891→	return nil
   892→}

   894→// treeNode represents a node in our tree structure.
   895→type treeNode struct {
   896→	entries map[string]*treeNode // subdirectories
   897→	files   []object.TreeEntry   // files in this directory
   898→}
   899→
   900→// BuildTreeFromEntries builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries.
   901→// Exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   902→func BuildTreeFromEntries(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   903→	// Build a tree structure
   904→	root := &treeNode{
   905→		entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   906→		files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   907→	}
   908→
   909→	// Insert all entries into the tree structure
   910→	for fullPath, entry := range entries {
   911→		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")
   912→		insertIntoTree(root, parts, entry)
   913→	}
   914→
   915→	// Recursively build tree objects from bottom up
   916→	return buildTreeObject(repo, root)
   917→}
   918→
   919→// insertIntoTree inserts a file entry into the tree structure.
   920→func insertIntoTree(node *treeNode, pathParts []string, entry object.TreeEntry) {
   921→	if len(pathParts) == 1 {
   922→		// This is a file in the current directory
   923→		node.files = append(node.files, object.TreeEntry{
   924→			Name: pathParts[0],
   925→			Mode: entry.Mode,
   926→			Hash: entry.Hash,
   927→		})
   928→		return
   929→	}
   930→
   931→	// This is in a subdirectory
   932→	dirName := pathParts[0]
   933→	if node.entries[dirName] == nil {
   934→		node.entries[dirName] = &treeNode{
   935→			entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   936→			files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   937→		}
   938→	}
   939→	insertIntoTree(node.entries[dirName], pathParts[1:], entry)
   940→}

   942→// buildTreeObject recursively builds tree objects from a treeNode.
   943→func buildTreeObject(repo *git.Repository, node *treeNode) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   944→	var treeEntries []object.TreeEntry
   945→
   946→	// Add files
   947→	treeEntries = append(treeEntries, node.files...)
   948→
   949→	// Recursively build subtrees
   950→	for name, subnode := range node.entries {
   951→		subHash, err := buildTreeObject(repo, subnode)
   952→		if err != nil {
   953→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   954→		}
   955→		treeEntries = append(treeEntries, object.TreeEntry{
   956→			Name: name,
   957→			Mode: filemode.Dir,
   958→			Hash: subHash,
   959→		})
   960→	}
   961→
   962→	// Sort entries (git requires sorted entries)
   963→	sortTreeEntries(treeEntries)
   964→
   965→	// Create tree object
   966→	tree := &object.Tree{Entries: treeEntries}
   967→
   968→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   969→	if err := tree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   970→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode tree: %w", err)
   971→	}
   972→
   973→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   974→	if err != nil {
   975→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store tree: %w", err)
   976→	}
   977→
   978→	return hash, nil
   979→}
   980→
   981→// sortTreeEntries sorts tree entries in git's required order.
   982→// Git sorts tree entries by name, with directories having a trailing /
   983→func sortTreeEntries(entries []object.TreeEntry) {
   984→	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
   985→		nameI := entries[i].Name
   986→		nameJ := entries[j].Name
   987→		if entries[i].Mode == filemode.Dir {
   988→			nameI += "/"
   989→		}
   990→		if entries[j].Mode == filemode.Dir {
   991→			nameJ += "/"
   992→		}
   993→		return nameI < nameJ
   994→	})
   995→}

   997→// collectChangedFiles collects all changed files (modified tracked + untracked non-ignored)
   998→// using git CLI. This is much faster than filesystem walk and respects all gitignore sources
   999→// including global gitignore (core.excludesfile).
  1000→//
  1001→// Uses git CLI instead of go-git because go-git's worktree.Status() does not respect
  1002→// global gitignore, which can cause globally ignored files to appear as untracked.
  1003→// See: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/129
  1004→//
  1005→// For the first checkpoint, we need to capture:
  1006→// - Modified tracked files (user's uncommitted changes)
  1007→// - Untracked non-ignored files (new files not yet added to git)
  1008→//
  1009→// The base tree from HEAD already contains all unchanged tracked files.
  1010→func collectChangedFiles(_ *git.Repository) ([]string, error) {
  1011→	ctx := context.Background()
  1012→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "status", "--porcelain")
  1013→	output, err := cmd.Output()
  1014→	if err != nil {
  1015→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git status: %w", err)
  1016→	}
  1017→
  1018→	lines := strings.Split(string(output), "\n")
  1019→	seen := make(map[string]struct{})
  1020→
  1021→	for _, line := range lines {
  1022→		if len(line) < 3 {
  1023→			continue
  1024→		}
  1025→
  1026→		// git status --porcelain format: XY filename
  1027→		// X = staging status, Y = worktree status
  1028→		staging := line[0]
  1029→		worktree := line[1]
  1030→		filename := strings.TrimSpace(line[3:])
  1031→
  1032→		// Skip .entire directory
  1033→		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(filename) {
  1034→			continue
  1035→		}
  1036→
  1037→		// Include if:
  1038→		// - Modified in worktree (Y='M')
  1039→		// - Untracked (XY='??')
  1040→		// - Added/modified in staging (X='A' or X='M') - these need to be captured too
  1041→		switch {
  1042→		case worktree == 'M': // Modified in worktree
  1043→			seen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1044→		case staging == '?' && worktree == '?': // Untracked
  1045→			seen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1046→		case staging == 'A' || staging == 'M': // Staged changes
  1047→			seen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1048→		}
  1049→		// Note: We skip deleted files (D) - those are handled via DeletedFiles parameter
  1050→	}
  1051→
